thread:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: P1 - model warmup failures: multiple hosts failing to load gpt-13b-quant during scheduled warmup. Errors include CUDA OOM, deserialization failure, and compile timeout. Paging on-call.
maria: acked. I'm on call, looking now. Any customer-facing alerts?
cs-ops: We're seeing a spike in inference errors for a small set of customers (3 customers, high QPS). Error rate up ~18% for the last 3m. CS is queuing incoming tickets.
alex: tagging in — grabbing logs from the failing task. Maria, can you confirm which pool this hit? dedicated-east-1-gpu-pool?
maria: yes dedicated-east-1, primarily nodes n-gpu-042 and n-gpu-045. Warmup job 2026-03-15-02:14.
priya: logs show repeated OOM at model deserialization step. Sample: ```E [2026-03-15T02:14:07Z] model_loader.cpp:421] cudaMemcpy failed: out of memory when allocating 2.1GiB for tensor buffer
Stack: load_model -> deserialize_weights -> allocate_device_buffers```
sam: also seeing compile timeouts after retrying. Link to compile job: https://ci.redwood.ai/compile/98765 (fails at step: kernel_jit -> timeout after 60s).
dmitri: CPU fallback wasn't configured for this model variant — loading policy is gpu_only. We should consider enabling fallback until we stabilize.
maria: mitigation plan in flight: 1) pause warmup autoscaler for the pool, 2) disable gpu_only for gpt-13b-quant (switch to gpu_preferred), 3) drain and reboot n-gpu-045 if it keeps failing, 4) roll forward a quantized-8bit variant if load continues to fail. Any objections?
alex: +1 on those. Also propose clearing the compile cache on the nodes before restarting so we don't hit the same compile timeout. Command: ```sudo rm -rf /var/tmp/compile_cache/* && systemctl restart redwood-runtime```
priya: note: compile cache clearing will briefly increase cold-start time for other models — CS aware?
cs-ops: CS notified customers on the affected accounts. They asked for ETA; we need to give a 30-60m window if we can't revert quickly.
maria: executing pause on warmup autoscaler now. paused by maria at 02:17.
incident-bot: Action: warmup-autoscaler paused (user: maria).
dmitri: I'm starting a graceful drain on n-gpu-045 and will reprovision to clear possible corrupted weights. If drain fails, I'll force-cordon and create a replacement.
alex: I've submitted a temporary routing policy to route 50% of traffic for affected customers to a smaller stable model variant (gpt-7b-quant) as a short-term fallback. Routing change ID: r-20260315-11.
priya: applying cpu fallback now for new warmup attempts (config change pushed). Should reduce OOMs for large deserializations.
maria: reboot of n-gpu-045 completed at 02:34. Post-reboot logs show one deserialization error then successful load on attempt 2.
monitoring-bot: Pager alert resolved for n-gpu-045 warmup failures (alert-id: warmup-1946-045).
alex: compile cache cleared on nodes n-gpu-042 and n-gpu-045. Re-triggered warmup jobs; monitoring for compile timeouts.
sam: still seeing 503 spikes for customers during the route switch, but error rate trending down from 18% -> 6% over 10m.
cs-ops: customers on the fallback variant are reporting degraded quality but service is stable. They're asking for postmortem and timeline to full restore.
maria: short incident summary for now: cause: large model deserialization + tight memory margins causing CUDA OOM and subsequent compile timeouts; contributing factor: gpu_only policy and stale compile cache. Impact: 3 high-QPS customers observed increased errors and degraded quality while routed to fallback. Mitigation: paused warmup autoscaler, enabled cpu fallback, cleared compile caches, restarted node n-gpu-045, routed 50% traffic to smaller model variant. Recovery: load stabilized by 02:36 with error rates returning below 2% for most customers.
dmitri: follow-ups I'm taking: (1) add safety memory headroom check to warmup controller, (2) make compile cache eviction resilient (avoid global cache wipe), (3) add a canary for deserialization OOMs.
alex: I'll open a PR to allow hot-fallback routing to smaller variants automatically when warmup fails x times: https://git.internal.redwood/pull/5421
priya: Ops notes: update runbook to include `sudo rm -rf /var/tmp/compile_cache/*` as a controlled mitigation, and document the tradeoffs.
maria: assigning postmortem owner -> alex. I'll hand off on-call to alex now. alex, you're on-call at 02:50.
alex: on-call acked. Taking over monitoring and follow-ups.
incident-bot: Incident transitioned to status: mitigated -> monitoring (owner: alex).
maria: offline to sleep. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
cs-ops: we'll consolidate customer comms and send a summary with mitigations + ETA for permanent fix.
alex: final notes recorded in incident tracker: https://incidents.redwood.ai/1946001234 (owner: alex; severity: P1; timeframe: 02:14-02:36). Postmortem ETA EOD tomorrow.
